content:
Maria Gonzalez: flagging an issue I hit while running e2e on staging — large tenants get routed into the same low-cost pool and we see p99 latency spikes during bursts. wondering if we can do a small policy tweak rather than full refactor
Kevin Li: ugh seen that. do we know if it's the model variant or the batching saturation?
Sasha Petrov: my read from traces: KV cache hit drops right before spikes, then batching window grows. looks like cold prefix + aggressive packing => large tail
Derek Choi: can we do 'slotting' that reserves micro-slots for bursty tenants? soft reservation that expires quickly?
Maria Gonzalez: exactly — soft reservation + preemptive window. idea: give a tenant N tokens worth of preemptive capacity per minute that doesn't affect weight calc unless used heavily
Kevin Li: sounds promising. tradeoff: we might slightly raise cost for underutilized slots. need a metric to gate it (p99 > threshold && cache_hit_rate < X)
Sasha Petrov: alternative: prioritize by recent cache-warmth instead of just tenant size. warmer prefixes get higher ephemeral weight. that preserves cost for cold noisy tenants
Derek Choi: sketch of policy DSL (very rough):
```
policy "soft_slotting" {
  when: request.region == client.region && p99_latency > 800ms
  allocate: ephemeral_slots = min(tenant.rate_limit, 1000)
  bump_weight: if cache_hit < 0.7 then +0.2
  ttl: 60s
}
```
Maria Gonzalez: love the TTL param. also we should include a preemption window so slots can be reclaimed if a higher tier request comes in
Kevin Li: preemption rules: tiered fallback. high tier -> steals from ephemeral_slots, medium -> steal from short-ttl buckets, low -> fallback to egress pool. we need a fairness clamp to avoid starvation
Sasha Petrov: fairness clamp suggestion: moving-average token consumption per tenant over 5m; cap steal to X% above baseline consumption. keeps burst handling bounded
Derek Choi: operational impact: telemetry needs new counters: ephemeral_slots_allocated, ephemeral_preemptions, slot_reclaim_latency. also add a trace tag on requests which used a reclaimed slot
Maria Gonzalez: agree. add alerts: rate(ephemeral_preemptions)>5/min AND p99>threshold -> rollback slotting policy automatically (circuit breaker)
Kevin Li: can we simulate with current load generator? I can run 10k concurrent synthetic tenants with mixed warm/cold prefixes and measure cost delta + p99 improvement
Sasha Petrov: I'll write an evaluator that toggles cache_warmth heuristics vs slotting and spits out cost/p99 CSV. include model variant mix (quantized vs fp16)
Derek Choi: infra-bot: deploy preview cluster 2026-11-slotting for load-testing please
infra-bot: ✅ preview cluster deployed: preview-2026-11-slotting, 6 nodes GPU-p4x, k8s-1.27. logs at https://ops.redwood/infralog/preview-2026-11
Maria Gonzalez: action items:
- Kevin: run synthetic load and capture baseline + slotting (due: 3d)
- Sasha: add evaluator + CSV outputs and compare cache_warmth heuristic (due: 4d)
- Derek: implement telemetry counters + trace tags in runtime (due: 5d)
- Maria: draft a short rollback/circuit policy and runbook (due: 2d)
Kevin Li: noted. I'll include cost-per-token delta and a simple ROC curve for p99 vs cost
Sasha Petrov: will include per-region breakdown, and a heatmap for eviction causes
Derek Choi: I'll PR the telemetry changes to eng-runtime with feature flag
Maria Gonzalez: OK. if the experiments look good we can roll to a few low-traffic tenants behind a canary flag before major rollout :shipit:
Kevin Li: :thumbsup: any objections?
Sasha Petrov: no objections from me. one caveat: we need to ensure the routing policy evaluation is cheap — can't add heavy compute to hot path
Derek Choi: agree. keep policy evaluation O(1) and rely on cached decisions where possible
Maria Gonzalez: thanks team — will check back in 72h with the runbook draft and initial results
